LME 3-month copper closing price rose by about 1.8% in the last tradin

g day of late 2012 compared to the first trading day in early 2012, or by 4.4% compared to the last trading day of late 2011. LME average prices of cash-month copper and 3-month copper were USD7,950/t and USD7,946/t in 2012, down by 9.87% and 10.05% y-o-y, separately. SHFE copper price had a similar trend with LME. SHFE copper price continued to rise pushed by market quotations during Chinese Spring Festival Holidays in Jan 2012 and hit the highest of 2012 on Feb 9, at 62,230yuan/t. SHFE copper price began to fall since Apr 2012 and hit the lowest of 2012, at 52,330yuan/t. Copper price stabilized and rebounded in late August. Copper price ever went back to over 60,000yuan/t thanks to the easing monetary policies from European Central Bank and a series of good news from FED’s QE3 and Germany's constitutional court ruling. After that copper price appeared another decline due to worries about economy and demand. Copper price had a rebounding sign in Mid-Nov and rose slightly in early Dec. SHFE 3-month copper closing price rose by 3.5% in the last trading day of late 2012 compared to the first trading day in early 2012, or by 4.4% compared to the last trading day of late 2011. SHFE average prices of cash-month copper and 3-month copper were 57,348yuan/t and 57,318yuan/t in 2012, down by 13.12% and 12.83% y-o-y, separately. **Average Copper Price on LME and SHFE in 2008-2012** ||**LME**（US

The most important influence factor is still economic situation in 2012. Other influence factors have negative impacts on refined copper prices, like China’s economy slowdown in the first three quarters of 2012, the European Sovereign Debt Crisis ups and downs, worries about US “fiscal cliff”, and so on. While easing monetary policies and Chinese improving economic data are most important factors to support the bounce and stabilization of refined copp

er price. The progress and doubts about global economy plays an important role on copper price changes. US dollar trend also makes a great influence on copper prices. The uncertainties of global economy and market risk aversion going up or down led to US dollar fluctuation, and then resulting in price fluctuations of bulk commodities priced in dollar. #### **Copper Market Commentary** ###### **1. Smelting/refining capacity continues to expand** Domestic copper smelting and refining capacity reached 4.07Mtpy and 7.13Mtpy by the end of 2011, separately. Newly added copper smelting and refining capacity will be 350ktpy and 930ktpy in 2012, with total smelting and refining capacity of 4.42Mtpy and 7.96Mtpy, separately. The main projects completed and put into operation in 2012 are 200ktpy copper smelting and refining project in Dongying Fangyuan Nonferrous Metals Group, 100ktpy in Yunnan Tin Group and reconstruction project of Fuchunjiang Smelting Co.. TLYS’s 400ktpy “double flash” project has been put off to 2013. Besides, Jinchuan Group’s 400ktpy copper refining project in Fangchenggang will be put into operation in 2013. It is estimated that newly added copper smelting and refining capacity will be 1.17Mtpy and 1.80Mtpy in 2013, with total capacity of 5.59Mtpy and 9.76Mtpy, separately. ###### **2. The great rise of imported and domestic produced copper conc. results in slight supply surplus** Domestic completed and commissioned copper mine production exceeded 100ktpy in 2012, including many expanding projects in JCCL, Duobaoshan copper mine in Zinjin Mining and so on. But actual newly-added copper mine capacity was about 70ktpy due to Dexing Copper Mine’s expanding projects commissioned in stages since 2009. Stockpiling demand for copper concentrates in newly-built smelters and refiners made domestic copper concentrates output keep a rising trend. According to data from CNIA, domestic www.antaike.com 3 Copper Monthly No. 193 copper-in-concentrate output was 1.492Mt in Jan-Nov 2012, up by 18.4% y-o-y, which still can’t meet the need of newly added smelting and refining capacity. In addition to the rising TC/RCs, copper concentrates imports began to increase greatly. Chinese imported copper concentrates was 6.893Mt (physical weight) in Jan-Nov 2012, up by 18.6% y-o-y. Copper concentrates supply surplus was mainly used in stockpiling for newly added capacity. Copper scraps supply in shortage** Copper scraps supply was in shortage in the whole 2012. Imported copper scraps had a y-o-y rise in 2012, but the purchasing cost was higher in 2012 than 2011. ###### **4. Copper cathode production keeps a rapid growth, but the growth rate of consumption continues to slide** According to statistics from NBS, domestic copper cathode production was 5.49Mt in Jan-Nov, up by 7.9% y-o-y. Data from CNIA showed that domestic copper cathode production reached 5.26Mt in Jan-Nov, up by 7.8% y-o-y. According to Antaike’s survey results, copper cathode production in domestic 12 producers amounted to 3.817Mt in Jan-Nov, up by 8.4% y-o-y. Among them, copper cathode production in JCC accounted for 28.40% of total output in domestic 12 producers; 20.93% in TLYS, 14.86% in Jinchuan Group and 8.61% in Yunnan Copper. So from above data, domestic copper cathode production kept a rapid growth trend. In terms of refined copper consumption, the growth rates of main copper end-using products saw slowdown or drop in varying degree, which led to a further fall of domestic demand for refined copper. Data from China Electricity Council still showed that during Jan to Nov, the completed power investment was 620.0 billion yuan, down 0.12% y-o-y. Among them, investment in power generation and grid was 302.1 billion yuan and 317.9 billion yuan, down 2.33% or 2.08% compared with the same period of 2011, respectively. Newly added power generation capacity was 57.30 GW in Jan to Nov, down 8.98 GW compared with the same period of 2011. 4 www.antaike.com Copper Monthly No. 193 According to State Electricity Regulatory Commission (SERC), total power consumption reached 413.93 TWh in Nov, up 7.6% y-o-y, hitting the new high since March of 2012. The national industrial power consumption increased by 7.0% y-o-y, 1.1 percentage points higher than Oct. The rally of industrial power consumption growth rate reflects the trend of economy development, especially in power-hungry heavy industry. Near the end of 2012, National Development and Reform Committee (NDRC) speed up the approval of new projects. On Dec 3 2012, NDRC approved 8 projects related to electric power, with dynamic investment of 11.37 bill

ion yuan. After that, NDRC approved 8 projects with power grid construction based and investment of 2.30 billion yuan. Electric power industry will still be the main copper consuming sector in the future, especially when the growth rates of refined copper consumption in property, air-conditioning and refrigeration and etc. industries are declining clearly. But it’s worth noting that about one third of the approved projects were badly behind schedule and many approved thermal power projects has not started construction. So, it needs a long time for theoretical good news to turn into actual effects. 

Air conditioning and refrigeration industry suffered a severe blow since early 2012, due to weak demand and high stocks. Production and exports of domestic refrigerators and air conditioners both had year on year drops and the latter are the main copper consuming products in this industry. 

Domestic property industry was in a downturn in the whole 2012, although there is an improving sign in Q3. The declining tendency can’t be changed in a short term and refined copper consumption in this industry will continue to be weak. 

Autos production growth resumed, but rail transit and ships manufacture were still not good. Refined copper consumption in transportation industry kept at a low growth rate. The growth rate in electronics industry slowed down or even drop. 

Data from NBS showed that among output of major copper-using end products, the year on year growth rate in refrigeration industry, autos and power cables increased in Jan-Nov 2012, while the output of power equipments, transformers, AC motors and etc. appeared different declines.

Chinese refined copper cons

umption temporarily can’t form an effective and continuous rising power for copper price. Refined copper imports and exports both create new high** Refined copper imports increased greatly in 2012, because there are a large plenty of financial copper, although LME refined copper price was higher than SHFE price and domestic refined copper stocks were high. Chinese annual imported refined copper created a new historical high based on higher average monthly imported refined copper in 2012, although monthly imported refined copper volume with over 400kt did not appear like that in Dec 2011. According to data from China’s Customs, imported refined copper reached 3.16Mt in Jan-Nov, 2012, up by 30.3% y-o-y. Chinese imported refined copper came back to a rational level as market paid more attention on high level of stocks in the bonded warehouse 6 www.antaike.com Copper Monthly No. 193 and partial domestic banks began to impose restrictions on financial copper. With regards to export, refined copper exports amounted to 249kt in Jan-Nov, 2012, up by 59.4% y-o-y, also creating a historical high. The rising refined copper exports were caused by following factors: firstly, rate adjustment on imported products with imported raw materials showed some effects; secondly, domestic refined copper supply was in surplus and LME copper was higher than SHFE. So completed capacity in 2013 may exceed that in 2012, and the expanding speed will be slowed down after 2014. It is estimated that domestic smelting and refining capacity will reach 5.59Mtpy and 9.76Mtpy in 2013, up 920kt and 1.40Mt compared to that in 2012. This will make Chinese refined copper production in 2013 continue to increase rapidly and reach 6.10Mt, up by 8.9% y-o-y. In terms of consumption, Chinese economy faced weak domestic and outside demand in 2012, with growth rate slowdown, which brought great pressure on copper consumption. The good effects to real economy brought by domestic all kinds of stimulus policies started in late 2012. It is estimated that economy situation in 2013 will be better than 2012 and copper consumption is expected to have a slight rally. Antaike estimated that Chinese refined copper consumption will be 8.10Mt in 2013, at a year on year rise of 5.5%, a little higher than 4.8% in 2012.

It is estimated that domestic imported copper concentrates will rise in 2013. Chinese imported copper scraps will continue to rise slightly. Refined copper imports will decline due to the restrictions on copper financing behaviors. On the whole, the increased production of refined copper will be higher than that of consumption in 2013; the gap between domestic refined copper production and consumption will be 2Mt, Domestic refined copper supply will be in surplus if imported refined copper is added in. 8 www.antaike.com Copper Monthly No. 193 With the coming of completion peak period of global copper concentrates projects, long term TC/RCs are expected to rise, with spot TC/RCs not too low. It is estimated that global economy will recover slightly in 2013, but with unbalanced recovery degree in different nations and regions. Copper price will fluctuate within a wide range in 2013, but it is hard to resume quickly.
